bullets.title: Brent crude surges 34% in July to $95/bbl on Iran escalation; Hormuz traffic craters
bullets.body: Brent crude hit $95/bbl (up from $71 on July 1, a ~34% move) as US-Iran military exchanges intensify, with oil vol spiking to 63. Hormuz transits fell to just 9 vessels vs. a historical 29, and European natural gas surged 5.5% on supply-risk fears. Shipping firms are paying massive bonuses to sailors willing to cross the strait.

bullets.title: Equity futures extend losses; real yields hit 2023 highs as bonds sell off alongside oil
bullets.body: S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 futures extended losses as rising oil collided with a bond market already under pressure—one account noted the 'equities bond shock' as yields push toward cycle highs on stretched growth pricing. Real yields on US 10-year Treasuries hit their highest level since 2023, and a Hedgeye macro note flagged 'Oil Up, Bonds Down = Quad3' as the dominant regime.

bullets.title: SPY first up day in 4 came on decelerating volume — weak conviction signal
bullets.body: SPY's lone up day over the prior four sessions occurred on volume that was decelerating vs. both 1-month and 3-month averages, suggesting the bounce lacked conviction.

bullets.title: NYSE margin debt +136% since Oct 2023 — fastest since dot-com bubble per Deutsche Bank
bullets.body: Deutsche Bank analysts warn NYSE margin debt has expanded 136% since October 2023, the fastest rate on record except for February–March 2000, partly attributable to the surprise dovish Fed pivot in December 2023.

bullets.title: Levered semiconductor ETF rebalancing created $6.5B MOC buy imbalance — largest in 1+ month
bullets.body: SOXL jumped 15.8% the prior session, generating an estimated $6.5 billion end-of-day MOC buy imbalance, the largest in more than a month. Inflows into levered ETFs are flagged as perpetuating the 'epic vol in high beta momentum.'

bullets.title: GEV misses EPS, beats revenue; FCF guidance nearly doubled — stock hits -10% premarket
bullets.body: GE Vernova reported Q2 EPS of $2.47, missing the $3.10 estimate, but revenue of $11.1B beat the $10.73B consensus. The company raised FY revenue guidance to $45.5B–$46.5B and nearly doubled its FY adj. FCF outlook to $11.5B–$12.5B from $6.5B–$7.5B. Despite the guidance raise, shares fell to session lows of -10% in premarket trading.

bullets.title: Mag 7 mixed premarket; NVDA underperforming chipmakers ahead of Alphabet & Tesla earnings
bullets.body: Premarket: GOOGL +0.8%, MSFT +0.4%, AMZN +0.2%, META flat, AAPL -0.3%, TSLA -0.3%, with NVDA underperforming the group as chipmakers broadly declined ahead of key earnings from Alphabet and Tesla.

bullets.title: Jensen Huang defends Chinese AI models, says US should NOT ban them
bullets.body: In an Axios interview, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang stated the US government should not ban or restrict Chinese AI models like Kimi K3, calling them 'excellent.' He advocated for using open-source models that are best-in-class, regardless of origin.

bullets.title: Reddit considers cutting off Google's $60M/year AI training data access
bullets.body: Reddit is reportedly weighing termination of Google's access to its content for AI model training, putting the $60 million-per-year deal struck in 2024 at risk. This would remove a key data pipeline for Google's AI development.

bullets.title: Bloomberg: AI sales beginning to justify data-center spending boom
bullets.body: Bloomberg reports that AI revenue generation is starting to validate the scale of hyperscaler capex buildouts, supporting the thesis that data-center infrastructure investment will be economically justified.

bullets.title: Economist warns AI backlash is in early innings and will intensify
bullets.body: The Economist flagged that social and regulatory resistance to AI adoption is growing and the AI backlash is 'only getting started,' representing a potential sector headwind beyond near-term earnings catalysts.

bullets.title: AT&T beats on wireless net adds (+432K vs. 325K est.) and EPS; maintains $18B+ FCF guide
bullets.body: AT&T Q2 results: wireless postpaid phone net adds of 432K crushed the 325K estimate, adjusted EPS of $0.65 beat the $0.59 estimate, and EBITDA of $12.38B exceeded the $12.1B consensus. Revenue of $31.6B was a slight miss vs. $31.77B. Company maintained FY FCF guidance of at least $18B.

bullets.title: Wells Fargo cuts ARM price target to $350 from $410
bullets.body: Wells Fargo reduced its ARM Holdings price target by $60 to $350, signaling reduced upside from prior levels.

bullets.title: MSFT flagged as cheap on valuation by fintwit account
bullets.body: At least one credible fintwit account called MSFT 'cheap' on current valuation ahead of upcoming earnings, a bullish contrarian signal given the recent market weakness.

bullets.title: TSLA seen pivoting to niche 1-2 passenger market; UBER better positioned at scale
bullets.body: One account argues Tesla is evolving toward the 1-2 passenger market (less than 1% of total auto sales), while Uber is already at scale and will benefit additively from 10-15 driverless partners on its platform — framing UBER as the structural winner in autonomous mobility.

bullets.title: Trump greenlights Saudi nuclear deal including potential uranium enrichment
bullets.body: The Trump administration formally approved a landmark civilian nuclear agreement with Saudi Arabia that opens the door to uranium enrichment within the Kingdom, a potential demand catalyst for US uranium producers.

bullets.title: Philadelphia Fed services survey: firm activity surges to +17.5; future expectations hit highest since Nov 2024
bullets.body: The Philadelphia Fed's July services sector survey showed firm-level activity jumped to +17.5 from +2.4 the prior month, while future business expectations surged to +41.9 from -0.3, the highest reading since November 2024. Services sector capex on equipment and software also hit its highest level since May 2022.

bullets.title: Photonics sector flagged as durable higher-beta semiconductor expression
bullets.body: One account highlighted LITE, AAOI, COHR, and NOK as established photonics plays positioned as higher-beta expressions of the semiconductor sector, calling the space 'here to stay.'

bullets.title: BEA methodology change expected to lower June core PCE by ~0.2 ppts
bullets.body: Upcoming BEA methodology revisions are anticipated to reduce measured June core PCE inflation by approximately 0.2 percentage points, a potentially meaningful downside surprise for the print.

bullets.title: Yen at 40-year lows despite authorities threatening 'bold' intervention
bullets.body: The Japanese yen continues to trade at levels last seen 40 years ago, with authorities' warnings of bold intervention failing to move the currency meaningfully — raising the stakes for any actual policy action.
